body:
The Shining Shores are a coastal region of Fein Uaill containing the Gates of Aelthor, a major city reached by sea. Their recovered history joins two scales of place: white streets, markets, and towers large enough to announce a civilization, and warm sand quiet enough for rest, friendship, and difficult political conversation.

Evidence boundary: this source establishes the city, shore, sea access, visual character, namesake, and several visits. It does not establish the population, exact age, current ruler, full extent of the coast, whether Aelthor founded the city, or whether every arrival in Fein Uaill passes through it.

The Gates of Aelthor

Tarwen of the Silver Star introduces the Gates as “our city on the shining shore.” The city’s white streets, bustling markets, and soaring towers immediately impress Elenia and Olokun. The account confirms a beautiful and active coastal city without converting that reaction into claims about its size, government, or wealth.

This is our city on the shining shore. We call it the Gates of Aelthor, after our first king after the breaking of the world.Tarwen of the Silver Star

Aelthor and the breaking of the world

Tarwen identifies Aelthor as Fein Uaill’s first king after an event remembered as the breaking of the world. The name turns the city into a civic memorial: every use recalls political continuity after catastrophe.

The account does not explain the breaking or state that Aelthor founded the city. Its wording may invite comparison with the Great Fracture, but the Codex does not identify the two events without direct evidence.

Aelthor, Aethor, and Arthor

The user confirms Aelthor as the proper spelling. Aethor and Arthor are alternate spellings of his name.

Arrivals by sea

On 10 January 2025, Elenia, Olokun, Draygar, Adelia, Scribonia, Eugene, Krone, and others reach the city. The Writer closes the arrival with white towers, grand shops, and sprawling civilization: “Welcome. To the Shining Shores.” Eldin Stormheart later rests on the warm sand beneath the setting sun, and Ithilrûnë Ailinor arrives by ship after him. Together these scenes establish sea access and multiple arrivals without making this the region’s only port.

15 October 2025 · the Heavenly Host

The Gates fall silent as Aionia’s Heavenly Host approaches beneath a cloud during an eclipse. Ships move downriver toward the sea, waves strike the walls, and radiant clouds swallow the red sky. Magnus, Adelia, Elenia, Scribonia, Olokun, Aria, and others assemble for the defense. The attack takes place on 15 October 2025, turning the coast into a battlefield.

A shore for difficult conversation

Elenia, Adelia, and Olokun later gather there while discussing Scribonia, Fein Uaill’s factions, the conflict with the dragons, and possible future diplomacy. The coast gives them a quieter place to discuss their plans for travel and diplomacy in the region.

22 December 2025 · departure into exile

After Bowene delivers Ciaránach’s verdict, Elenia, Olokun, and Aravil are told to meet at the Shining Shores before sunset. The coast becomes the threshold between judgment and the Babel-Ashur campaign: an escort point, a farewell site, and the last place in Fein Uaill before an exile intended to remain revisable rather than permanent.

People in the recovered record

  • Tarwen of the Silver Star introduces the city and preserves the explanation of its name.
  • Elenia and Olokun react to the city’s beauty and later meet along the shore.
  • Adelia joins the shoreline conversation about factions, dragons, Scribonia, and diplomacy.
  • Eldin Stormheart rests on the warm sand after arriving in Fein Uaill.
  • Ithilrûnë Ailinor arrives by ship while seeking the mysterious land and greater power.

The open record

The Gates’ population, founding, exact age, present ruler, civic structure, full battle losses, and relationship to other Fein Uaill cities remain unrecovered. The full geographic extent of the Shining Shores, Aelthor’s biography, and the identity of the “breaking of the world” also remain open.

Holding the wall, counting the loss

Before the Heavenly Host reaches the shore, the last ship leaves the lighthouse ahead of the storm. Aria’s ship remains visible under its flag for a moment before she docks and takes her place. The soldiers finish forming on the walls while the sea and the radiant clouds close around them.

An immense incarnate later strides out of the clouds and strikes toward the spellcasters, bending time around itself. The defense wavers. A cosmic burst takes Olokun out and makes even Pride reel; ultimately Olokun delivers the last blow, and the attacker is unmade into dust.

The narration describes hundreds, perhaps thousands, dead. It gives no complete casualty list. Aria climbs above the rubble and the soldiers cheer her bloodied blade. The battle’s full account keeps that successful defense beside its losses and the argument about another war that follows.

Sunset and a channel of contact

Bowene’s exile judgment turns the shore into a departure point with a deadline. Elenia is required to leave; Aravil and Olokun are named in the company, and others may choose to accompany them. Escorts are arranged for sunset. Not everyone who travels thereby receives the same compulsory sentence.

Bowene also offers information, supplies and a sending stone for the struggle in Babel-Ashur. His judgment and the departure therefore preserve both punishment and continued cooperation. The coast is the place where that separation becomes a journey. The offer of a door left open supplies no fixed date or automatic legal permission for return.
